title: Preflight policy adapter for VPC Terraform pipelines — OPA/Conftest integration and live migration checks
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Add a reusable 'policy adapter' step to Redwood's VPC Terraform CI/CD pipelines that runs OPA/Conftest checks against terraform plan output and performs migration safety analysis for module upgrades and stateful changes. The adapter should: (1) consume a standardized terraform plan JSON or tfplan, (2) execute curated Conftest/OPA policies (security, networking, cost, and data-plane impact), (3) surface human-friendly failure reasons with remediation hints, and (4) provide an extensible scoring/allowlist mechanism so on-call and platform engineers can tune gating sensitivity. Additionally the adapter will run a migration health analyzer to detect high-risk changes to stateful resources (subnet CIDR changes, route table swaps, RDS/network endpoints) and surface rollout strategies (canary apply, emergency rollback playbook) as pipeline artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline includes a 'policy-adapter' step that accepts terraform plan JSON and exits non-zero on policy violations
Conftest rules for critical failures (data-plane, public exposure, KMS misuse) cause pipeline fail; medium-risk rules mark 'warning' but still report detailed remediation guidance
Adapter emits a machine-readable report (JSON) with: rule id, severity, human message, file/line hint (where available), suggested remediation steps

Module upgrade/migration analyzer flags changes that require manual approval (e.g., subnet CIDR shrink, route table replacement, changes to managed database endpoint) and annotates the PR with recommended rollout strategy
Pipeline integrates with GitHub Checks: failing checks block merges; warnings are visible in check annotations
Performance: adapter completes Conftest evaluation for a typical VPC plan (<5k lines) under 90s in CI runner with 2 CPU/8GB RAM
Documentation and runbook published: how to add rules, how to exempt changes, and how to interpret reports
Security review completed and KMS/HSM handling for plan artifacts validated
implementation_tasks: Design policy-adapter interface (inputs: tfplan/tfjson, env: workspace, vars; outputs: report.json, annotations)
Upgrade our terraform-plan-to-json converter in CI to ensure stable tfjson output (use 'terraform show -json')
Author initial Conftest policies: network-exposure.rego, kms-usage.rego, iam-broad-rego, cost-estimate.rego
Implement scoring engine: map policy severities to pipeline outcome (fail/warn/pass) and provide allowlist mechanism by module/resource
Build migration analyzer heuristics: detect resource replacement, IP range shift, rds endpoint change, and high-risk terraform 'taint' events
Integrate with GitHub Checks API to post annotations and attach report.json
Add CI job that caches policy bundles and periodically pulls policy updates from policy-repo
Create rollout playbook templates for flagged migrations (canary steps, test harness, rollback commands)
Add e2e tests: sample VPC plans with expected fail/warn/pass outcomes; test GitHub annotation flow
Open PR with implementation, run in 'shadow' mode for two cycles, gather false-positive metrics, iterate
notes: Decision: Use Conftest running OPA as the core policy engine to leverage existing rego skillset across platform teams
Trade-off: Conftest is fast to iterate but some complex cross-resource analysis may require custom Python analyzers; we'll implement heuristics in adapter and keep regulatory checks in rego
We will ship with a conservative rule-set (fail only for unambiguous security/data-plane misconfigurations) and expose a policy tuning dashboard in the console in a follow-up
We must handle TF state-sensitive operations carefully: any check that infers data migration requires manual approval by default
Storing tfplan JSON in CI artifacts requires KMS encryption at rest; coordinate with Security on key usage and short-lived artifact retention
risks_mitigation: False positives slowing merges: shadow run for 2 cycles, collect FP rate; provide quick bypass for urgent releases with audit logging
Leak of sensitive values in plan JSON: ensure plan export uses -json and we run 'sensitive' scrubber that replaces known secret patterns and removes provider credentials
Policy drift between environments: maintain a single policy repo and pin policy bundle versions in pipeline; auto-update via scheduled job after manual review
Runtime flakiness in CI: run adapter with resource limits and timeouts; if adapter exceeds threshold mark as 'warning' and allow manual retry
test_plan: Unit tests for each rego rule with Conftest harness
Integration tests: run full pipeline against a fixture VPC 'safe' plan and 'unsafe' plan in CI
Performance benchmark: measure adapter runtime on typical plan sizes and optimize cache/bundle loading
Manual QA: platform engineer reviews annotations on several real PRs during shadow period
Security review: confirm artifacts encrypted and ephemeral; confirm no secrets persist in PR comments
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (shadow): Merge adapter into CI with mode=shadow for all private-deployments repos (2 cycles) — collect metrics and false positives
Phase 2 (opt-in): Enable adapter as optional 'preflight' check that posts comments but does not block merges for a select tenant repo group
Phase 3 (gate): Flip to blocking for critical repos (platform-managed infra), require review for exceptions
Fallback: Provide a one-click bypass in the pipeline UI that requires a short justification and creates an audit ticket
Post-rollout: schedule a policy retro every 6 weeks to tune and add new checks
